name: Autonomous Evaluation and Refinement of Digital Agents
description: We show that domain-general automatic evaluators can significantly improve the performance of agents for web navigation and device control. We experiment with multiple evaluation models that trade off between inference cost, modularity of design, and accuracy. We validate the performance of these models in several popular benchmarks for digital agents, finding between 74.4 and 92.9% agreement with oracle evaluation metrics. Finally, we use these evaluators to improve the performance of existing agents via fine-tuning and inference-time guidance. Without any additional supervision, we improve state-of-the-art performance by 29% on the popular benchmark WebArena, and achieve around 75% relative improvement in device control settings.
reputation: Widely used in the web-agent community as a standardized environment and benchmark suite for evaluating browser-based agents.
notes: Primarily an evaluation framework/ecosystem rather than a single benchmark; scores vary substantially across included tasks and setups.
